summary.intent: Fix failing desktop E2E tests on the fix/desktop-e2e-sequence-mismatch branch after web E2E was already passing.
summary.outcome: Identified a FUSE publish queue stale-inode bug (deleted inodes not removed from publish_queue causing 'Folder inode not found' on flush), fixed it in both macOS and Windows write_ops, and committed the changes.

repo: The 'FilePointer not found' / 'Folder inode not found' desktop E2E failure pre-dates PR #448 and was already failing as of April 2.
The FUSE layer maintains a publish_queue that is not cleaned up when inodes are removed via rmdir, unlink, or rename-over-destination — this causes stale-inode errors on flush.
Both macOS (crates/fuse/src/write_ops.rs) and Windows (crates/fuse/src/platform/windows/write_ops.rs) had the same missing cleanup pattern.
The desktop E2E test (tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/test-round-trip.sh) creates and deletes temporary directories, which exercises the stale publish_queue path.

code.finding: handle_rmdir and handle_rename (destination inode removal around line 914) do not purge the removed inode from publish_queue, leading to 'Folder inode not found' on next flush.
Same missing publish_queue cleanup on inode removal; pattern located via grep for fs.inodes.remove.
Round-trip test script exercises create+delete directory sequences that trigger the stale publish_queue bug.

workflow: CI E2E job can be manually triggered against a branch after push to validate targeted fixes.
Grepping for fs.inodes.remove was an effective strategy to find all inode-removal sites needing publish_queue cleanup.

friction: Desktop E2E failure was a pre-existing regression (failing since April 2) mixed in with PR #449's changes, making it harder to distinguish new breakage from old.
Required investigating both macOS and Windows platform-specific write_ops files separately for the same bug pattern.
open_items: handle_unlink publish_queue cleanup was noted as 'defensive' — verify whether files can actually appear in publish_queue and whether the unlink path needs the same fix.
The underlying cause of why the publish_queue accumulates stale entries without TTL or flush-based GC may warrant a broader audit.
CI run result for the committed fix was not yet confirmed in the transcript — outcome of the new CI run is unknown.
